$comment: Operator-maintained slot map for the optical rip tower.
Keyed on `firmwareSerial` — the drive's own serial, read from MakeMKV's
DRV: line. It is unique per physical drive and is RETAINED across a
firmware reflash, which matters here: slots 2-4 are LG drives running
OmniDrive firmware that makes them report as ASUS, so the model string
cannot identify them but the serial can.
`usbPortPath` and `bridgeSerial` are CACHED HINTS, not identity. The
daemon refreshes them whenever it sees a drive, and repairs them from the
firmware serial after a re-cable. Never hand-edit them to force a mapping.
Slots are physical tower order, top = 1 to bottom = 9, established
2026-07-24 by ejecting each drive and having the owner call out the slot.
Correlation verified 2026-07-24: slot order maps monotonically onto USB
port path, which is what makes the port path a trustworthy runtime key.
`/dev/srN` appears nowhere in this file on purpose — it reshuffles on
every USB re-enumeration and is never identity.
`readOffsetSamples` is the drive's AccurateRip read offset, in samples,
measured ONCE per physical drive with `cyanrip -f` and then true
forever: it is a property of the drive itself, so it survives a
re-cable and a `/dev/srN` reshuffle precisely because this file keys on
the serial. null means nobody has measured it yet — a supported state,
not an error: the rip simply runs without `-s`, and AccurateRip answers
"not in database" on every disc.
NEVER fill it in from a model lookup. AccurateRip publishes offsets by
MODEL, so that shortcut is the obvious one — and here it would hand an
ASUS offset to three LG drives, for the same reason this whole file is
keyed on the serial. Procedure: measure once with `cyanrip -f` per drive.
$towerRootComment: Everything below this port path shares one long (10 m) active USB
extension into one physical 10-port hub. The hub internally cascades
4-port chips, which is why sysfs shows a 3-tier tree where the rack has
one hub. A fault at or above this node hits ALL drives, and the known
single point of failure is the extension's aux power: run passively the
repeater is undervolted and the whole bank drops. Keep it plugged in —
the new cable has a power-indicator LED, so that check is now at a glance.
Path was 2-1.1.2 until 2026-07-30, when the tower moved back to the
original mobo USB3 port on a new cable (per-drive usbPortPath hints below
self-repair from the firmware serial; do not hand-edit them). See
